To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the user’s mental model is a critical factor in determining how the user interprets online and offline help, and the user’s mental representation of help is a major contributor to the occurrence of errors.
users of online library catalog systems commit errors because they: (1) have misconceptions; and (2), when they have misconceptions, they are unable to use help effectively.

the design features that make online systems difficult for users include (1) the lack of a consistent, predictable, and intuitive interface, (2) the lack of an explicit, consistent, and intuitive search process, and (3) the lack of explicit, consistent, intuitive, and unambiguous help.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the design of an online library catalog system can affect the user’s mental processes and how the user’s mental representations can in turn affect his or her interactions with the system.
how the design features of online library catalogs contribute to the occurrence of errors.
how users of online library catalogs learn to use the systems and the errors they make as part of that learning process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

users’ errors are not simply the result of a lack of knowledge, but rather the product of a complex interplay of factors, including: (1) incorrect mental representations of the system; (2) a lack of knowledge about the system; (3) a lack of experience with the system; (4) the user interface of the system; and (5) the user’s mental model of the search task.
the LCS system is a complex and difficult one to learn, and that it is not a system in which users can be confident that they can recover from their mistakes.
the LCS online catalog system is not a user-friendly system, and the user is responsible for the errors he or she makes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the user interface of LCS is not well designed. It does not provide adequate support to users to help them recover from errors.

users’ mental models of online library catalogs are often incomplete, and that the online help and instructions provided by the system do not provide sufficient information for users to correct these mental models.
users of online library catalog systems are likely to make errors, and the nature of the errors will depend on the mental models they bring to the task.
The main takeaway from our work is that

users of online library systems need to be trained to understand the underlying structure of these systems, to develop an accurate mental model of how these systems function, and to be able to recognize and correct errors.

users’ mental representations of online and offline systems are critical to their ability to use these systems effectively and that the design of help systems and other instructional materials should take into account these mental representations.
the design and evaluation of help systems for online library catalog systems should take into consideration how users mentally represent and interpret help and instructions.
